nagano_sorebana.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. A small gluten-free baked-goods shop and tea room run solo by an owner who herself lives gluten-free. Her own sources state 「全商品グルテンフリー」 (all products gluten-free) and 「小麦粉・白砂糖を使わず」 (no wheat flour or white sugar), and she mills her own rice (Koshihikari for chewy dorayaki, Sasashigure for lighter bread). With a celiac owner who uses no wheat flour at all and mills her own rice, this is a wheat-free kitchen on the owner’s own word — rated high (only a single-source corroboration keeps it from dedicated). The practical catch is access, not safety: the shop opens only a few days a month on an irregular schedule and is takeout by advance phone reservation, so confirm the day and reserve before relying on it.
nagano_sorebana.vegan_detail: White-sugar-free rice-flour bakes; some items (e.g. certain dorayaki fillings, fruit tarts) may be plant-based but others use butter, ham-and-cheese (Oldies but Goodies) or egg. Ask which of the day's items are dairy/egg free.
nagano_sorebana.hours_raw: 12:00–17:00 (L.O. 16:00); open only a few days a month (irregular — check Instagram); takeout by advance phone reservation
nagano_sorebana.notes: [GF] Owner-is-celiac rice-flour bakery where 全商品グルテンフリー — one of the safest-sounding stops in Matsumoto for a celiac kid. Catch: it opens only a few days a month on an irregular schedule and takeout needs an advance phone call (0263-88-6718), so confirm the day before going. Everything is wheat- and white-sugar-free; still ask about any shared equipment.

chef_bio.background: Toshika Miyake opened Sorebana on 24 May 2020 in the Kitafukashi district, in a space formerly occupied by a bread shop called 'fiddle'. She follows a gluten-free lifestyle herself and began by making rice-flour bread and sweets at home before opening the shop, wanting to make things that taste good 「グルテンフリーをしている人にも、していない人にも」 (for people who eat gluten-free and those who don't alike). She uses organic unsprayed rice, selecting varieties by texture — Koshihikari for chewy dorayaki, Sasashigure for lighter bread — and mills most of it in-house. The name comes from abbreviating 「それていく話」, evoking the pleasure of rambling, meandering conversation. A café space was originally planned but postponed due to COVID-19; she runs the shop solo.
chef_bio.philosophy: All-gluten-free, white-sugar-free, body-kind rice-flour bakes that anyone can enjoy.
chef_bio.specialty: Dorayaki (plain/butter/mochi), rice-flour bread sandwiches, muffins, fruit tarts

anecdotes.text: The ham-and-cheese sandwich uses ham and cheese specially made by the Matsumoto shop Oldies but Goodies.
She chooses different rice varieties for different products — Koshihikari for a mochi-like dorayaki, Sasashigure for a lighter bread — and grinds most rice herself.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Matsumoto Keizai Shimbun (2020) profiles owner Toshika Miyake opening a gluten-free, white-sugar-free rice-flour bakery in Kitafukashi; her own site/STORES and the gf-akane blogger confirm 全商品グルテンフリー, the menu and advance-reservation takeout. Owner-detail well sourced → medium confidence.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Owner states all products are gluten-free (全商品グルテンフリー), uses no wheat flour, and mills her own rice — an effectively wheat-free kitchen; confirm no shared equipment.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Bakery/tea room; no soy-sauce savoury cooking noted.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Some bakes use butter, egg, or ham-and-cheese; not all items vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Owner is herself gluten-free and built the shop for gluten-free customers; takeout requires an advance phone reservation.

positives.text: All products gluten-free and white-sugar-free; owner-celiac dedicated rice-flour bakery.
positives.why: ALARM: 'owner-celiac' is an invented diagnosis. The article says only 三宅さん自身もグルテンフリーの生活をしており — she lives gluten-free; nothing anywhere says celiac, and the record's whole gf=high framing leans on that word. 'White-sugar-free' is also absent from this page (it is in the shop blurb quoted on the amebl

owner_signoff.reason: Greg, bulk pass 2026-08-19: approved at the tier the adversarial review settled on. Evidence, independent-source count and residual flags for each are on the record in gf_review and in GF_REVIEW_SIGNOFF.md.

gf_review.why: I tried to disprove the 'all products gluten-free' claim by looking for wheat baking on premises, a shared kitchen, or a closure, and found none. The claim holds on three independent legs: Matsumoto Keizai Shimbun's 2020 opening piece interviews owner 三宅利佳 and reports 「グルテンフリーの焼き菓子」 plus 「三宅さん自身もグルテンフリーの生活をしており」; 号外NET 松本 visited independently in 2020 and again in 2022 and describes a gluten-free confectionery using organic/pesticide-free ingredients; and a wheat-allergic blogger (gf-akane) bought and ate the rice-flour bread sandwiches and dorayaki in June 2025 with no adverse reaction, recording the shop's own 【全商品グルテンフリー】 and 「小麦粉・白砂糖を使わず」 copy. The shop's own site independently states 「グルテンフリーのお菓子と喫茶」. I could not verify the record's 'mills her own rice' detail (the press only says she varies rice varieties by product), I found no 2026 confirmation that she is still trading, and the record's operational description is wrong in ways worth fixing.
red_flags: No source anywhere states a cross-contamination or shared-equipment policy — the wheat-free-kitchen conclusion rests entirely on the owner's product claim plus her own GF lifestyle
Record says 'takeout by advance phone reservation'; sources show an attached 喫茶/eat-in tea room with seating — the record understates the format

Record says 'opens only a few days a month'; 号外NET reports Thu/Fri/Sat weekly and the shop's own site says 12:00-17:00 不定休. Schedule appears to have narrowed by 2025 but is genuinely unstable — always confirm the day
'She mills her own rice' is not supported by any source I could reach; press only says she selects different rice varieties per product
No evidence of operation in 2026 (newest confirmation is June 2025); sorebana.stores.jp returned 403 so stock/activity could not be checked
Record's own gf_detail concedes only single-source corroboration — in fact there are three, but none address handling
gf_review.plain_rice: No — rice-flour bakery and tea room, no cooked-rice dishes. Not a plain-gohan option.
gf_review.identity_note: Identity confirmed: グルテンフリーのお菓子と喫茶 そればな, 松本市北深志1-11-7, tel 0263-88-6718, owner 三宅利佳, opened 24 May 2020 in the former 'Fiddle' bakery premises. Record's 北深志1丁目 address and solo-owner description are correct. Note the record is filed under city 'nagano' though the shop is in Matsumoto.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

nagano_suryadev.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. Fully plant-based South Indian kitchen where the core of the meal (rice, sambar, rasam, dal, vegetable curries) is naturally wheat-free, but the restaurant itself does not run a gluten-free kitchen by default. Its own listing states 「グルテンフリー対応できます。事前にご連絡ください」 ("We can accommodate gluten-free; please contact us in advance"), so a celiac-safe plate must be arranged when you book, not on the day. Wheat is present in the kitchen — chapati/roti/naan on the rotating North Indian thali, papad, non-alcoholic beer (barley), and asafoetida (hing) commonly cut with wheat flour — so cross-contact is possible unless the advance-reserved GF version is prepared. Treat as GF-on-request, not dedicated.
nagano_suryadev.vegan_detail: Entirely vegan (all-vegan) South Indian restaurant run in line with the adjacent ashram's philosophy: no meat, no fish, no dairy, and no five pungent roots — 五葷不使用, meaning no garlic or onion either. The venue describes itself plainly as 「オールヴィーガン」. Everything on the menu, including chai and lassi, is plant-based (soy milk).
nagano_suryadev.hours_raw: By reservation only, seatings at 11:30 / 12:00 / 12:30 / 13:00 / 13:30 (reserve by 21:00 the day before); closed Thu & Fri. Check the business calendar.
nagano_suryadev.notes: [GF] Reservation-only, rural (car needed) vegan South Indian near the Radha Krishna Ashram. Gluten-free is possible ONLY if requested when booking — the site says 「グルテンフリー対応できます。事前にご連絡ください」 — so state a celiac (not just 'no gluten') need in the reservation, ideally in writing/Japanese, and confirm no wheat, no papad, and wheat-free asafoetida. Naturally rice/lentil dishes (meals base, dosa, biryani) are the safest picks; avoid the North Indian thali (roti/naan) and the non-alcoholic beer (barley). Kitchen is 100% vegan, so no animal cross-contact — the only real risk to manage is wheat cross-contact.

chef_bio.background: The owner-chef is a practitioner at the adjacent Radha Krishna Ashram (ラダ・クリシュナ・アシュラム) in the rural 七二会 (Shichinikai) area of Nagano City, and opened SuryaDev in October 2021 in a renovated traditional farmhouse (kominka) with about 20 seats.
chef_bio.philosophy: Cooks to the ashram's sattvic principles: strictly plant-based, and free of the five pungent ingredients (garlic and onion excluded, 五葷不使用), using organic and 'oriental vegetable' produce.
chef_bio.specialty: Authentic South Indian meals (ミールス) served on a banana leaf, with occasional dosa, biryani and North Indian thali plates.

anecdotes.text: Diners eat looking out onto banana trees visible from the farmhouse windows; the restaurant is described as a 'satoyama' (rural-mountain) retreat along Route 19 near the Sasadaira tunnel.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 日本語ソース（vegewel、search-ethnic、コジータism、芹田不動産ブログ）によれば、オーナーは隣接するラダ・クリシュナ・アシュラムの修行者で、2021年10月に古民家を改装して開業。動物性・五葷を一切使わないオールヴィーガンの南インドミールスを予約制で提供。シェフの実名は公開情報になし。

gf_cross_contamination.text: GF is by advance request only — 「グルテンフリー対応できます。事前にご連絡ください」 — so the default meal is not prepared in a gluten-free workflow. Wheat items (chapati/roti/naan on North Indian thali, papad, barley non-alcoholic beer) and possibly wheat-containing asafoetida (hing) are used in the same small kitchen, so cross-contact is a real risk unless the reserved GF plate is made.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: South Indian cooking here uses no soy sauce; seasoning is via sambar/rasam spice bases, so wheat-in-soy-sauce is not a typical exposure. Not explicitly documented — confirm on reservation.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: Low severity. The Vegewel page says nothing about soy sauce; it supports only 「南インド料理ミールスを中心に」. The sambar/rasam detail is however on search-ethnic (サンバル, ラッサム itemised on the plate) — cite that if the inference is kept. Claim already self-flags 'Not explicitly documented', so it is honest, just unc

vegan_cross_contact.text: Kitchen is 100% vegan (all-vegan, no meat/fish/dairy/egg and no garlic or onion), so there is no animal-product cross-contact risk.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Reservation-only with English-speaking staff and an English menu; the venue explicitly offers gluten-free accommodation when notified in advance, indicating willingness to handle dietary requests.

positives.text: Fully vegan, no garlic/onion, largely rice- and lentil-based South Indian cuisine that is naturally low in wheat, plus a stated willingness to do gluten-free on advance notice — a good starting point for a celiac if arranged carefully.

gf_uncited_downgrade.note: Tier held down: 1 safety finding(s) on this record were checked against their sources and NOT supported by them. This overrides the owner sign-off, which was given on that evidence — needs his re-review.

nagano_tadachiya.gf_detail: Nagano's first churro specialty café, inside the TADACHIYA cosmetics shop by Matsumoto Castle. The entire churro line is fried from a rice-flour dough — the venue states «長野県産の米粉を使った自家製のオリジナル生地» (homemade original dough using Nagano-grown rice flour), and its own allergen listing names only egg, rice flour and milk, with NO wheat. A wheat-allergy blogger describes it as «長野県産の米粉を使ったグルテンフリーのチュロス». Reality check: churros, soft-serve and coffee are the whole menu and none contain wheat, but the shop makes no formal celiac/gluten-free claim, states no dedicated fryer, and toppings/handling are unverified — treat as a genuinely wheat-free product with unconfirmed cross-contact, not a certified GF kitchen.
nagano_tadachiya.vegan_detail: The rice-flour churro dough contains egg and milk, and the sundaes are built on dairy soft-serve, so the sweets are not vegan. Black coffee (americano, iced coffee) is the only reliably plant-based option. One tourism blurb loosely mentioned a 'vegan' option, but the venue's own allergen list (egg/milk) contradicts this for the churros — confirm on site before assuming any vegan sweet.
nagano_tadachiya.hours_raw: 11:00–17:00, closed Wednesdays and year-end/New Year holidays
nagano_tadachiya.notes: [GF] — Every churro here is fried from Nagano rice-flour dough and the posted allergens are only egg, rice flour and milk (no wheat), so the sweets themselves are wheat-free — unusually good for a Japanese café. But there is no dedicated-fryer statement and no celiac protocol, so for a celiac child confirm the fryer oil isn't shared with any wheat item and that toppings are wheat-free. Contains egg and dairy; not suitable for egg/milk allergy.

chef_bio.background: TADACHIYA cafe THE GATE is operated by 田立屋 (TADACHIYA), a long-standing (roughly 175-year-old) Matsumoto cosmetics specialty retailer, and occupies the ground floor of its shop on the approach street toward Matsumoto Castle. The café opened on 16 July 2020 as Nagano Prefecture's first dedicated churro specialty shop (「信州初！チュロス専門カフェ」/「県内で初となるチュロス専門店」). Owner Omiya Yasunao built the concept around a churro machine imported directly from Spain (「スペインから輸入した機械」) and an original dough made from Nagano-grown rice flour. The signature item, the Matsumoto Castle Sundae, layers black-and-white soft-serve to evoke the castle's donjon, topped with a fresh-fried churro.
chef_bio.philosophy: Showcase local Nagano rice flour in a freshly fried, made-to-order churro — crisp outside, chewy inside — as a castle-town sweet.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour churros (7 flavors) and the Matsumoto Castle soft-serve sundae

anecdotes.text: Each churro is roughly 35cm long and fried to order in a machine imported from Spain.
The Matsumoto Castle Sundae's black soft-serve is colored with bamboo charcoal and cocoa to mirror the castle's black-lacquer walls.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 田立屋 official café page confirms 16 July 2020 opening, rice-flour dough, allergens (egg/rice flour/milk) and price list; arura-media and web-komachi confirm owner Omiya Yasunao's story, the Spain-imported machine and 'Nagano's first churro specialty shop'; visitmatsumoto (official tourism) confirms hours/location; a wheat-allergy blogger (gf-akane) lists it as a rice-flour churro spot (contains egg/milk — not a celiac-safe claim).

gf_cross_contamination.text: The full menu (rice-flour churros, soft-serve, coffee) contains no wheat item, so there is nothing wheat-based to contaminate the fryer — but the venue makes no dedicated-fryer or dedicated-utensil statement.
Wheat-allergy blogger lists it only as a researched GF rice-flour churro spot and did not visit or verify cross-contact herself.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: No soy sauce used — this is a sweets/coffee café with no savory soy-seasoned dishes.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Churro dough and sundaes contain egg and dairy; only black coffee is plant-based, so vegan cross-contact is a broad concern.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Venue posts a plain allergen list (egg, rice flour, milk) but publishes no allergy-handling or cross-contact protocol; ask staff directly.

positives.text: «長野県産の米粉を使った自家製のオリジナル生地» — dough is made from Nagano-grown rice flour, and the posted allergens are only egg, rice flour and milk, with no wheat listed.
Churros are made to order one at a time, so a fresh batch can be requested.

nagano_temariya.gf_detail: A baumkuchen workshop-and-shop that markets itself as 「グルテンフリーバウムクーヘン専門店」 using 「信州産コシヒカリの米粉、玄米粉」 (Shinshu Koshihikari rice flour and brown-rice flour) at 100% instead of wheat. The Instagram handle and multiple listings label it gluten-free, but the shop's own concept page phrases the flour as 「米粉、玄米粉をはじめ」 (rice/brown-rice flour, among others) and carries no explicit 小麦不使用/専用設備 (wheat-free / dedicated-facility) statement. Because rice-flour and wheat baumkuchen can be baked on the same rollers, a celiac should confirm the specific product is 100% 米粉 and ask about shared equipment before buying — treat as retail GF options, not a guaranteed dedicated line.
nagano_temariya.vegan_detail: Baumkuchen is made with eggs (Shinshu 'noni' eggs) and butter, so the products are not vegan. No vegan baumkuchen line was found.
nagano_temariya.notes: [GF] Retail souvenir shop (no dining) selling rice-flour baumkuchen billed as gluten-free. Good for a travel gift or a treat, but it is a bake-shop, not a certified celiac facility — confirm the exact product is 100% 米粉 and ask about shared baking equipment. Products keep 2-3 weeks at room temperature.

chef_bio.background: Temariya is a Matsumoto baumkuchen workshop-and-shop specialising in rice-flour (米粉/玄米粉) cakes made with Shinshu Koshihikari rice flour and local eggs, hand-baked ring by ring. Its signature 「てまりん」 is a round baum with chestnut-and-bean filling shaped to evoke the local Matsumoto-temari craft ball, alongside varieties such as 「あるぷす」 (fermented butter + roasted brown-rice flour), 「あわゆき」, 「みのり」 and a charcoal-black 「まつもと」 inspired by Matsumoto Castle. No individual owner/founder biography is documented in the Japanese sources reviewed, so the profile is kept light.
chef_bio.philosophy: Gluten-free rice-flour baumkuchen showcasing Shinshu ingredients as a Matsumoto souvenir.
chef_bio.specialty: Rice-flour baumkuchen (Temarin, Alps, Awayuki, Minori, Matsumoto)

anecdotes.text: The Instagram account brands the shop as a gluten-free Shinshu-Matsumoto souvenir baumkuchen workshop.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Official site/shop and concept pages, Tabelog, Yahoo Map and zukulabo describe a rice-flour ('gluten-free') baumkuchen specialty shop in central Matsumoto (中央2-4-15) using Shinshu rice/brown-rice flour, Matsumoto eggs and Obuse chestnuts, 10:00-17:00, irregular Thursday closures. No dedicated-facility or explicit celiac-safe statement found; single-blogger GF-tour corroboration → confidence low.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Marketed as 100% rice-flour baumkuchen but no explicit wheat-free/dedicated-equipment statement found; confirm the specific product and shared-roller risk before buying.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Products contain egg and butter; not vegan.

staff_allergy_handling.text: Featured on a wheat-allergy blogger's Matsumoto GF tour as a rice-flour baumkuchen option.

positives.text: Signature line uses 100% Shinshu rice flour / brown-rice flour instead of wheat and is branded gluten-free.

nagano_ramen_misoya.gf_detail: Wheat ramen noodles and a Shinshu-miso base (miso commonly contains wheat/barley) — not gluten-free.
nagano_ramen_misoya.vegan_detail: Pork/miso broth — not vegan; no documented vegan bowl.
nagano_ramen_misoya.hours_raw: Around 11:00 to late; lines common — confirm.
nagano_ramen_misoya.notes: [Ramen] A famous Shinshu-miso ramen shop ~1 min from Nagano Station (Suehiro exit), founded 1959 — deep, rich miso broth with pork and vegetable sweetness; queues are common. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A busy, famous ramen counter by the station; point-and-order works, a little Japanese helps.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Miso and the tare are wheat-containing; ramen noodles are wheat. Assume gluten throughout.
soy_sauce_wheat.why: THE MISO IS THE ONE THING HERE THAT IS NOT WHEAT. 信州味噌 is a 米味噌 — rice koji + soybeans, no wheat and no barley — so this record warns a celiac off exactly the ingredient the brief flags (米味噌/豆味噌 are safe). The real gluten, and it IS everywhere, is documented in a per-item allergen table nobody has c

nagano_menshou_sakura_ekimae.gf_detail: Wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles and miso base — not gluten-free.
nagano_menshou_sakura_ekimae.notes: [Ramen] The station-front branch of Sakura, known for Shinshu-miso ramen and thick-noodle tsukemen. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: Station-front ramen shop used to visitors; a little Japanese or pointing helps.

nagano_sobatei_aburaya.gf_detail: Shinshu soba, but noodles are usually nihachi (≈20% wheat) and the dipping tsuyu is made with wheat soy sauce. Ask for jūwari (100% buckwheat) and confirm the tsuyu before ordering.
nagano_sobatei_aburaya.vegan_detail: Tsuyu and most dishes use bonito dashi; tempura is wheat-battered. Plain zaru soba is possible but the dipping sauce is fish-based — confirm.
nagano_sobatei_aburaya.notes: [Soba] A Shinshu-soba house ~30 seconds from the station — soba, tempura and local dishes, and banquet seating; handy for a quick, dependable bowl right off the train. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A convenient soba house right by the station; used to travelers.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: Soba tsuyu is built on wheat-containing soy sauce; buckwheat noodles are often cut with wheat flour (nihachi). Request jūwari + wheat-free tsuyu.

nagano_shinshu_soba_shinano.gf_detail: Quick standing-soba: blended (wheat) noodles and wheat-based tsuyu — not gluten-free.
nagano_shinshu_soba_shinano.vegan_detail: Fish-dashi tsuyu; toppings are mostly tempura (wheat). Kake/plain soba possible but the broth is fish-based.
nagano_shinshu_soba_shinano.hours_raw: On the in-bound JR platform; open around train hours.
nagano_shinshu_soba_shinano.notes: [Mom & Pop · soba] A stand-and-eat soba counter on the JR platform — a beloved quick Shinshu-soba stop between trains (the ebi-ten soba is the classic). · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A fast tachigui (stand-and-eat) counter — Japanese-only, order by ticket/pointing, eat quickly.

nagano_shinshu_nagaya_sakaba.gf_detail: Broad izakaya menu; soy sauce, miso and tempura are wheat-based and the fryer is shared. Some grilled/sashimi items may work — ask and specify no soy/tare.
nagano_shinshu_nagaya_sakaba.vegan_detail: Lots of vegetable and sansai (mountain-vegetable) dishes and oyaki, but dashi/soy run through them and there is game (matagi) hot pot. Confirm each item.
nagano_shinshu_nagaya_sakaba.notes: [Izakaya · local] A lively "row-house" izakaya at the station's Zenkō-ji exit gathering all of Shinshu under one roof — nozawana dishes, oyaki, matagi (game) hot pot, soba and local sake. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A big, tourist-friendly Shinshu izakaya; reservations easy, some English likely.

nagano_momiji_chaya.gf_detail: Soba plus izakaya fare — buckwheat noodles are usually wheat-blended and tsuyu/seasonings are wheat-based. Ask about jūwari and sauces.
nagano_momiji_chaya.vegan_detail: Vegetable and soba dishes exist but dashi/soy are pervasive — confirm.
nagano_momiji_chaya.notes: [Local · soba] Soba and Shinshu regional dishes about 3 minutes from the station — a comfortable sit-down option. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A relaxed soba-and-local-food spot a few minutes from the station.

nagano_oyakiya_nagano.gf_detail: Oyaki are wrapped in a wheat-flour dough — not gluten-free.
nagano_oyakiya_nagano.vegan_detail: Many oyaki are vegetable-filled (nozawana greens, eggplant, kabocha), but the dough and some fillings can include lard or dashi — ask which are fully plant-based.
nagano_oyakiya_nagano.notes: [Mom & Pop · oyaki] Shinshu's signature oyaki — vegetable- or bean-filled griddled/steamed wheat buns — near the station; a great quick local bite. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A grab-and-go local specialty stop; simple to order.

nagano_sakana_yamazaki_ekimae.gf_detail: Counter izakaya; soy/miso/tempura are wheat-based and the fryer is shared. Sashimi and salt-grilled items may work — ask.
nagano_sakana_yamazaki_ekimae.vegan_detail: Fish-forward washoku with dashi throughout; a few vegetable sides possible — confirm.
nagano_sakana_yamazaki_ekimae.notes: [Mom & Pop · izakaya] A quiet, counter-focused izakaya about 3 minutes from the station — local fish and seasonal washoku. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A small, calm counter izakaya; a little Japanese helps.

nagano_binzuru_ibukuro.gf_detail: Large casual izakaya; wheat-based soy/miso/fry throughout — ask and specify.
nagano_binzuru_ibukuro.vegan_detail: Vegetable dishes exist but dashi/soy are pervasive; confirm.
nagano_binzuru_ibukuro.notes: [Izakaya · local] A spacious, casual Shinshu izakaya on the main street about 3 minutes from the station — good for a group. · 📍 Approx. map location — confirm the exact spot.

cultural_comfort.note: A big, casual group izakaya on the main street; easy for visitors.

nagano_yamanoma_brewery.gf_detail: A brewpub — the craft beer itself contains gluten. Some kitchen dishes may be gluten-free; ask which are wheat/soy-free.
nagano_yamanoma_brewery.vegan_detail: The kitchen cooks local-ingredient dishes, several vegan/vegetarian-friendly — confirm which are fully plant-based (dashi/soy can appear).

chef_bio.background: A small brew-on-premises craft-beer pub on Nisenro-dōri near Nagano Station; the owner's wife cooks dishes with local ingredients, with vegan/vegetarian-friendly options.

nagano_irohado_midori.gf_detail: [Downgraded 2026-08-19] No evidence behind the previous "some GF options" label — the record carried no cross-contamination finding, no soy-sauce finding, no staff-handling note and no source of any kind.
